**How to keep your data safe — a practical backup routine right now**

---

### 1️⃣ Adopt a **hybrid backup strategy**  
Combine the convenience of automatic cloud sync with a reliable local copy.  
*Cloud protects you from laptop loss or fire; a local copy protects you from cloud‑service outages or account problems.*  [[concepts/backup‑strategy]]

| Layer | What it does | Typical tool |
|------|--------------|--------------|
| **Primary (cloud)** | Continuous, hands‑free upload of new files. | **Google Photos**, **iCloud**, **OneDrive** (or any service you already use) [[concepts/cloud‑backup]] |
| **Secondary (local)** | Keeps an offline, version‑controlled copy. | **Windows File History**, **FreeFileSync**, external drive mirroring [[concepts/local‑backup]] |

---

### 2️⃣ Set up the **plug‑and‑forget local mirror**  
1. **Create a permanent “Photos Incoming” folder** on your computer. Dump everything from phone or camera there immediately after each trip or daily import. [[concepts/incoming‑folder]]  
2. **Enable cloud sync** on that folder (e.g., OneDrive or Google Photos) so every file is uploaded in the background. [[concepts/cloud‑backup]]  
3. **Mirror the folder to an external drive** with an automatic tool:  
   * **Windows File History** – runs automatically whenever the drive is attached. [[entities/file-history]]  
   * **FreeFileSync** (if you prefer more control) – schedule a daily job. [[entities/freefilesync]]  
   This “plug‑and‑forget” mirroring gives you a second copy without any extra manual steps. [[concepts/plug‑and‑forget‑backup]] [[concepts/external‑drive‑mirroring]]

---

### 3️⃣ Run a **monthly health check** (quick, 5‑minute routine)

#### iPhone (iCloud)  
1. Settings → *your name* → **iCloud → iCloud Backup** – note the *Last successful backup* date.  
2. Verify **iCloud Photos**, **Notes**, and **Messages in iCloud** are enabled. [[entities/icloud]]  
3. Add a test photo or note, then check it appears on **iCloud.com**.  

#### Android (Google)  
1. Settings → **System → Backup** – confirm the *Last backup* timestamp under **Google One**. [[entities/google-one]]  
2. In **Google Photos**, ensure **Backup** is on. [[entities/google-photos]]  
3. In **Google Keep**, pull‑to‑refresh and verify a new note syncs to **keep.google.com**. [[entities/google-keep]]  
4. Add a test photo/note and confirm it shows up on the web.

*If any “last‑backup” date is stale or counts of items differ between device and cloud, investigate the service’s error messages.* [[summaries/session-07_2024-06-15]]

---

### 4️⃣ Keep your folder structure tidy (helps future restores)  
Name each trip folder with **date‑place** (e.g., `2025‑02 Japan`). [[concepts/trip‑folder‑naming]] This makes locating a specific set of files trivial, whether you’re browsing the cloud or the external drive.

---

### 5️⃣ Optional: Periodic **duplicate removal**  
After each import, run a quick scan (FreeFileSync, built‑in duplicate finder, or a script) to delete obvious junk or exact copies. [[concepts/duplicate‑removal]]

---

## TL;DR checklist you can copy‑paste

```
☑ Set up “Photos Incoming” folder → cloud‑sync enabled
☑ Activate Windows File History (or schedule FreeFileSync) → external drive mirroring
☑ Monthly: 
   – iPhone → Settings → iCloud → Backup → verify dates & test item
   – Android → Settings → System → Backup → verify Google One timestamp
   – Google Photos / Keep → ensure backup on, test new item
☑ Rename each trip folder as YYYY‑MM Place
☑ Run duplicate‑removal pass after each import
```

Following this routine gives you **continuous, automated protection** plus a **redundant offline copy**, satisfying best‑practice backup principles from both of our past sessions.
